This is a single snapshot read of the whole struct xdp_desc — the kernel-side canonical pattern. It complies with the invariant (validated copy == used copy), assuming READ_ONCE of the struct is a single read — for a 16-byte struct, READ_ONCE is not necessarily atomic, but that's upstream behavior as well; not a variant.

2. xsk_umem_consume_tx (net/xdp/xsk.c lines 173-198): peeks desc via xskq_peek_desc into a kernel-stack `struct xdp_desc desc`, validates via xskq_validate_desc, then uses desc.addr/desc.len — validated copy used. Complies.

3. xsk_generic_xmit (lines 233-281): len = desc.len; skb allocated; addr = desc.addr; buffer = xdp_umem_get_data(xs->umem, addr); skb_store_bits(skb, 0, buffer, len). All uses come from the local desc copy that was validated in xskq_validate_desc. Complies. Note: desc.addr was validated to be within umem size and within a single chunk (addr+len within same chunk), and skb was allocated with len bytes — so no OOB.

4. The drivers (i40e_xsk.c i40e_xmit_zc line 753; ixgbe_xsk.c ixgbe_xmit_zc line 642) use xsk_umem_consume_tx outputs (dma, len) — kernel-side values derived from validated local desc copy. No direct UMEM rereads in drivers.

One subtlety worth considering for the negative result: xskq_validate_desc's `*desc = READ_ONCE(ring->desc[idx]);` — READ_ONCE on a struct (16 bytes: u64 addr, u32 len, u32 options). READ_ONCE for sizes > 8 bytes uses a memcpy-based copy via __READ_ONCE_SIZE which does memcpy. The compiler could in theory still split it... but READ_ONCE wraps with volatile semantics preventing tearing/coalescing. This is the same pattern the upstream kernel uses to this day (xskq_validate_desc is unchanged in current kernels modulo xskq_valid_desc checks). So it's the canonical safe pattern, not a variant.

Another point: xsk_generic_xmit uses desc.len for skb allocation and desc.addr for the UMEM read — both from the validated local copy. Safe.

Also xsk_umem_consume_tx uses xskq_produce_addr_lazy(umem->cq, desc.addr) — local copy. Safe.

One more potential candidate to note: in xskq_validate_addr (FQ), `*addr = READ_ONCE(ring->desc[idx]) & q->chunk_mask;` — single read, masked, then validated (addr < q->size). Safe.

And in the drivers, `xsk_umem_peek_addr` returns handle into a local u64, validated (xskq_is_valid_addr in xskq_validate_addr) before use in xdp_umem_get_data/xdp_umem_get_dma. Safe.

Note the interesting historical bug: xsk_umem_peek_addr_rq (include/net/xdp_sock.h line 102-111) returns `rq->handles[rq->length - 1]` from the reuse queue — a kernel-owned array, not user-shared. Safe (kernel memory). Though later kernels masked the handle... in i40e_alloc_buffer_slow_zc, `handle &= rx_ring->xsk_umem->chunk_mask;` — applied in driver. ixgbe_alloc_buffer_slow_zc also masks. But reuse queue entries were validated when originally produced. Kernel-owned. Safe.

Also worth noting: i40e_alloc_buffer_zc (non-rq path, line 343-356) uses handle from xsk_umem_peek_addr without additional masking — but xskq_validate_addr already masked with chunk_mask and checked < size. Safe.
